title: OrchBench: Evaluating Multi-Agent Orchestration Plans in Isolation via Deterministic Simulation
claims: Deterministic simulation can isolate orchestration-plan variables from worker/tool/environment noise.
The reported benchmark correlates with a tested Claude Code cohort; this remains a research result, not a universal performance guarantee.
unresolved_questions: How well does the benchmark transfer to coding tasks, ARM/Android execution, and long-horizon workflows?
Can its task DAG representation map cleanly to the monorepo manager tournament schema?
provenance_notes: Primary research source; preserve paper version and do not promote benchmark scores into model rankings.

title: NIST IR 8536 Supply Chain Traceability: Manufacturing Meta-Framework
claims: The final framework provides an interoperable approach for linking and verifying traceability information and emphasizes provenance, pedigree, cryptographic linkage, and selective disclosure.
NIST reports an open-source Python reference implementation associated with the framework.
unresolved_questions: How should selective-disclosure traceability map onto software/model runtime evidence and SBOM/AIBOM records?
What is the final public reference-implementation release state?
provenance_notes: Primary NIST source; final publication date 2026-09-09.

title: Android / ARM local inference evidence lane
claims: llama.cpp provides a FOSS local inference baseline suitable for CPU/quantized runtime experiments; the monorepo now adds a device/runtime evidence contract rather than treating any model/runtime as a permanent route.
unresolved_questions: Which ARM64 Android devices and backends should be admitted to the first reproducible cohort?
Which energy/thermal measurement method is sufficiently portable?
provenance_notes: This record is an evidence-lane anchor, not a claim that all Android backends are supported equally.

title: NVIDIA OpenShell / Open Agent Safety Platform
claims: NVIDIA describes OpenShell as open-source runtime software that governs agent execution, access, inference destinations, and policy enforcement.
The associated platform announcement describes an open software/reference-system approach to agent safety and governance.
unresolved_questions: Cross-platform portability beyond NVIDIA's reference infrastructure needs validation.
Which policy and audit artifacts should be normalized into the monorepo admission contract?
provenance_notes: Official NVIDIA product and press-release sources observed 2026-09-30.

title: AIP: Agent Identity Protocol for Verifiable Delegation Across MCP and A2A
claims: The paper proposes invocation-bound capability tokens for verifiable delegation across MCP/A2A/HTTP.
The reported experiments evaluate delegation, provenance binding, and adversarial cases; these are research results from one paper, not ecosystem-wide measurements.
unresolved_questions: Independent replication and standardization path.
Integration with established workload identity and OAuth systems.
Constrained-device overhead and key-management behavior.
provenance_notes: Primary research source; preserve research status and paper identifier.

title: Cerebras + Gimlet Cloud heterogeneous inference announcement
claims: Cerebras and Gimlet announced integration of wafer-scale compute into Gimlet Cloud.
The companies state a target of up to 3,000 tokens/second and a first Cerebras-powered datacenter later in 2026; these performance/deployment figures are attributed company claims.
unresolved_questions: Independent performance validation on agent workloads.
Total-task latency after orchestration and placement overhead.
Energy and memory tradeoffs versus local/ARM inference.
provenance_notes: Primary company announcements observed 2026-09-30; Reuters retained as secondary context in the dated briefing.

title: OpenTelemetry GenAI/MCP semantic conventions
claims: The MCP semantic-conventions document is explicitly marked Development.
The conventions define MCP-specific spans/metrics and warn that prompt variables and tool arguments/results may contain sensitive information.

Which GenAI/MCP attributes stabilize enough for the canonical monorepo schema.

title: Model Context Protocol 2026-07-28 Specification
claims: The 2026-07-28 MCP release establishes a stateless protocol core and retires the protocol-level initialize/initialized handshake and Mcp-Session-Id.
The release adds Multi Round-Trip Requests, header-based routing, authorization hardening, an extensions framework, and updated SDKs.
unresolved_questions: Which repository MCP integrations still assume protocol-level sessions?
Which application-level state handles should be represented in canonical evidence without reintroducing hidden transport state?
provenance_notes: Primary MCP maintainer release post; pin protocol version 2026-07-28.

title: Scanning the Harness: Supply-Chain Defects in AI Coding-Agent Configurations
claims: The study analyzed 3,171 public GitHub repositories with AI coding-agent configurations.

The reported validated findings include unpinned MCP servers, pre-approved arbitrary execution, and shell-preauthorizing skills; the paper reports 16.0% of studied setups carrying a security defect under its decidable rules.
unresolved_questions: How representative are the studied repositories of private/enterprise agent configurations?
Which additional vulnerability classes are outside the paper's decidable rules?
How should an agent lockfile encode permissions as well as versions and hashes?
provenance_notes: Primary research source; preserve methodology and do not interpret the 16.0% figure as ecosystem-wide compromise probability.

title: AgentCompass v1.0.0
claims: AgentCompass v1.0.0 provides open-source agent evaluation infrastructure with trajectory, tool-call, usage, latency, analyzer, and artifact support.
The project separates model, benchmark, harness, and environment concerns for reproducible evaluation.
unresolved_questions: Which benchmarks transfer cleanly to Termux/ARM64 constraints?
Which artifact subset should become the monorepo canonical evaluation receipt?
How should benchmark outputs be joined to ATES without conflating speed with quality?
provenance_notes: Official repository release note observed 2026-10-03; pin v1.0.0 for experiments.

title: CODESTRUCT: Code Agents over Structured Action Spaces
claims: CODESTRUCT evaluates code agents operating over named AST entities rather than raw text spans.
Across reported SWE-Bench Verified experiments, the paper reports 1.2–5.0 percentage-point Pass@1 improvements and 12–38% lower token consumption for most tested models.
unresolved_questions: Replication with the monorepo's own task cohorts and languages.
How structural action interfaces interact with existing patch/review tooling.
Whether the reported gains persist under multi-agent orchestration.
provenance_notes: Primary research source; reported gains are benchmark-specific and not a universal guarantee.

title: Photonic accelerators for AI across cloud and edge platforms
claims: The Perspective maps cloud- and edge-oriented photonic accelerators and identifies energy efficiency, throughput, density, and latency opportunities.
It also identifies scalability, electro-optic interface losses, nonlinearities, reconfigurability, and optics footprint as material constraints.
unresolved_questions: When do photonic systems become economically competitive for general inference workloads?
Which compiler/runtime abstractions can keep photonic backends optional?
What benchmark fields capture energy and memory movement fairly across heterogeneous accelerators?
provenance_notes: Peer-reviewed Nature Photonics Perspective; version of record 2026-09-15.
